core_obligations: Note that the 'only if' direction is clear and assume M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) is finitely generated (proof lines 25204-25205).
Write each generator as a sum of simple tensors to conclude that M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) admits a finite generating set consisting of elements of M (proof lines 25205-25208).
Conclude that there is a morphism from a finite free R-module to M whose cokernel is killed by tensoring with R' oplus R_f (proof lines 25209-25210).
Apply the Beauville-Laszlo faithful statement to this cokernel to deduce that M is finitely generated (proof lines 25211-25212).
Conclude that the last statement about R^wedge is a special case of the first by the same-quotients statement (proof lines 25213-25214).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an element f, and a ring map R -> R' inducing isomorphisms R/f^nR -> R'/f^nR' for n > 0, and asserts that an R-module M is finitely generated if and only if the (R' oplus R_f)-module M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) is finitely generated; a special case with the completion is recorded as an example (source lines 25189-25201). The proof begins by noting that the 'only if' direction is clear, so it assumes M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) is finitely generated (proof line 25204-25205). The substantive step is a manipulation of generators: writing each generator as a sum of simple tensors, the module M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) admits a finite generating set consisting of elements of M (proof lines 25205-25208). That is, there is a morphism from a finite free R-module to M whose cokernel is killed by tensoring with R' oplus R_f; applying the Beauville-Laszlo faithful statement to this cokernel gives that M is finitely generated (proof lines 25209-25212). The final sentence observes that the completion example is a special case of the first statement by the same-quotients statement (proof lines 25213-25214). The non-routine content is the observation that the generating set can be chosen inside M itself, which turns the hypothesis into a statement about the cokernel of a finite free presentation of M.
